title: Release-prep fails when CHANGELOG Unreleased carries a breaking-change marker and the chosen bump is patch-level (mirror of quest-cli QCLI-328)
description: Filed on opum-agent's dispatch (OPAG-665 AC2, 2026-09-28). ADR read by ref: opum-doc docs/adr/gate-release-prep-on-a-breaking-changelog-entry-at-a-patch-bump.md at 724fc0959f0b (blob 9fc3ecde). quest-cli's QCLI-328 gates its release-prep on its own CHANGELOG; lore-cli mirrors it over lore's CHANGELOG.md. Because lore and quest share one version (constitution Article 3 clause 1), a breaking entry in EITHER changelog forces the pair's bump. Read QCLI-328's implementation by ref before building, and match its marker vocabulary and verdicts.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Lore release-prep fails (non-zero, message naming the entry and the bump) when CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] carries a breaking-change marker and the chosen bump is patch-level, and passes on the same tree at a minor/major bump -- proven both ways on ONE tree
The breaking-change marker vocabulary and verdicts match quest-cli QCLI-328, read by ref and cited with its SHA; any difference is named and agreed with quest-cli
How a break in quest-cli's changelog forces lore's bump (the shared version) is stated and either enforced or explicitly left to the pairing, per the ADR
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers any scripts/ or release.yml change

plan: scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs: port quest-cli's QCLI-328 rule (BREAKING_HEADING, bumpLevel, notes-section selection) read at bee16361, with one parser tolerant of Keep-a-Changelog [Unreleased]/[X.Y.Z] and quest's bare headings

Same module reads quest-cli CHANGELOG.md by ref (gh api --hostname github.com, raw media type, default ref dev, --quest-ref override), injectable for tests; an unreadable or zero-section changelog refuses
release.yml: new breaking-bump job beside version-parity (no if/needs, sparse checkout, GH_TOKEN), publish needs it; package.json check:breaking-bump; runbook step
test/lcli632-breaking-bump-gate.test.ts: one-tree proofs for lore side, quest side and unreadable quest changelog, plus the real tree; mutation-test the patch comparison
implementationNotes: ORCHESTRATOR RULING on AC3 (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-28): ENFORCED, not left to the pairing. Per the ADR's Consequences (opum-doc docs/adr/gate-release-prep-on-a-breaking-changelog-entry-at-a-patch-bump.md, main), the check runs against BOTH changelogs before either side releases. Lore's release-prep also reads quest-cli's CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] BY REF (GitHub API on quest-cli's dev, or the paired release ref) and applies the same marker-vs-patch rule, and it FAILS if it cannot read it (an unreadable changelog is not a clean one). quest-cli files the mirror follow-up. Its per-repo gate, whose vocabulary AC2 matches, is opum-ai/quest-cli#367 (QCLI-328). Re-read the ADR by ref when starting, since this is a relay; the ADR is the binding record.

NEXT STEP -- write scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs per the plan. Design notes found so far: test/release-workflow.test.ts's LCLI-616 existsSync check strips only a parity/ prefix, so the new job should sparse-check-out at the workspace root (no path:) rather than a new subdirectory. A mid-task AC2 course correction from the dispatching session (legacy **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:** marker handling plus one CHANGELOG.md edit) was received; this agent's attempt to record it on this task was refused by the permission classifier, so it is NOT on this record and the dispatching session should record it from its own seat.

ORCHESTRATOR RULING on AC2 (opum-agent, cross-session, 2026-09-28 ~18:30Z; recorded by the parent session because the implementer's write was refused by the permission classifier). (1) quest-cli's '### ... (breaking)' heading is the canonical marker. (2) check-breaking-bump must FAIL, at any bump level, when the checked notes section contains lore's legacy bold '**BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:**' marker, and the message must name the canonical spelling; otherwise the gate reads lore's existing style as 'no breaking change'. (3) Prove on one tree: canonical marker at a patch bump -> red; legacy marker -> red naming the canonical spelling; clean entry -> green; canonical at minor -> green. The relay said 'without a major bump'; the parent reads that as 'at a patch bump' per the ADR (minor suffices) - confirm with opum-agent if in doubt. Scope consequence: the implementer owns one CHANGELOG.md edit - move the LCLI-612 bullet in [Unreleased] under a new '### Changed (breaking)' heading, dropping the bold prefix. OPEN (from the implementer, 2026-09-28): the released [0.11.0] section also carries a '**BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:**' bullet, so a no-flag run against package.json 0.11.0 goes red under a literal reading; the gate only matters at release prep for the NEXT version, so the parent's inclination is to scan only the section for the version being released and leave released sections as history - confirm before coding.

ORCHESTRATOR RULINGS settling the two open points (cross-session, 2026-09-28; binding): (A) 'Without a major bump' means what the ADR says -- at least a minor bump is required; only a patch-level bump is refused. (B) Scan only the section for the version being released ([Unreleased], or the '## [X]' section once the bump is in); released sections are history and are never scanned.

Mutation test (2026-09-28): mutated the patch-level comparison in scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs (level === 'patch' -> 'major'). Predicted 8 of 20 tests red — exactly the ones asserting the patch-level problem (one-tree patch, bare-heading patch, finalized patch, both-markers count, quest-side patch, real-tree, and the two stubbed-CLI patch cases); legacy-marker, unreadable, zero-sections, usage, bump-level and clean-entry tests stay green. Actual: 8 fail / 12 pass, the identical 8. Restored; 20/20 green.

Implementation complete on feat/LCLI-632-breaking-bump-gate (2026-09-28): scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs + .d.mts; test/lcli632-breaking-bump-gate.test.ts (20 tests, quest read stubbed/injected, no network); release.yml breaking-bump job beside version-parity (sparse checkout at workspace root of /package.json, /CHANGELOG.md, /scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs; --quest-ref main; publish needs it); package.json check:breaking-bump; runbook step 3 note after item 2; CHANGELOG.md: LCLI-612 bullet moved under ### Changed (breaking), bold prefix dropped, released sections untouched. Real-tree proofs: --next 0.11.1 -> exit 1 (lore read 28 sections, ## [Unreleased] breaking, 0.11.0 -> 0.11.1 patch refused; quest read 11 sections from opum-ai/quest-cli@dev, clean); --next 0.12.0 -> exit 0; --next 0.12.0 --quest-ref main -> exit 0. No-flag run -> exit 1 with 'package.json still names 0.11.0 -- pass --next' hint. AC1, AC2, AC3 checked by the implementer with evidence (2026-09-28). AC1: one real tree both ways -- node scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs --next 0.11.1 exited 1 naming '## [Unreleased]' and '0.11.0 -> 0.11.1 is a patch bump'; --next 0.12.0 exited 0. AC2: BREAKING_HEADING and bumpLevel are byte-for-byte quest-cli's read at bee16361 (a test pins the regex source/flags); the differences (tolerant heading parser, released sections never scanned, the legacy BEHAVIOUR CHANGE marker refusing at any bump level) are named in the script header and were settled by orchestrator rulings recorded above. AC3: ENFORCED -- the checker reads quest-cli's CHANGELOG.md by ref (gh api, github.com pinned, default dev, --quest-ref main in release.yml) and refuses an unreadable or zero-section one; proven by stubbed tests and a real read (11 sections at dev and main). AC4 left unchecked: bun test (4540 pass, 1 skip, 0 fail) and bun run lore check exit 0 are proven, but the reviewer pass over scripts/ and release.yml has not run yet.

REVIEWER CHANGES-REQUIRED resolved (2026-09-28, second commit on the branch). Finding 1 (HIGH, certification hole): the non-empty-[Unreleased]-beats-own-section priority let a patch bump pass when the version's own '## [X]' section carried a breaking heading and [Unreleased] held one clean leftover note; quest's gate at bee16361 prefers the own section (own !== -1) and exits 1 on identical bytes. Finding 2 (inverse false positive): bump-in with non-empty [Unreleased] set previous = the version itself, redding with a misleading 'X -> X' self-patch. Finding 3 (LOW): 'released sections are never scanned' overstated — in the stale-tree window (no --next, package.json still names a released version) the released top section IS the checked one. FIX: adopted quest's section selection verbatim (own section when it exists, previous = the versioned section below it; else Unreleased, previous = the first versioned section); removed the self-patch message suffix (now unreachable); corrected the script header (items 2 and 4) and the release.yml step comment; --quest-ref=main equals form now accepted. Tests changed: renamed 'ruling B ...' to 'an older section's breaking or legacy markers do not bind the current bump, and previous is the section below it' (adds previous 1.5.0 assertion); added the 'the version's own section wins over [Unreleased] (quest parity; reviewer findings)' describe with the two reviewer-named hybrid cases (breaking own + clean leftover -> patch red; clean own + breaking [Unreleased] -> green, previous naming the section below); rewrote the real-tree test for the stale-tree window; added the --quest-ref=main equals-form CLI test. SUPERSEDED RECORDED OUTPUT: the earlier note's 'no-flag exit 1 with 0.11.0 -> 0.11.0 self-patch + --next hint' belonged to the removed priority and no longer occurs. NEW real-tree outputs: --next 0.11.1 -> exit 1 (lore: '## [Unreleased] carries a breaking heading, but 0.11.0 -> 0.11.1 is a patch bump'; lore read 28 sections; quest read 11 from opum-ai/quest-cli@dev); --next 0.12.0 -> exit 0; no-flag -> exit 1 (lore: '## [0.11.0] - 2026-09-27 carries lore's legacy **BEHAVIOUR CHANGE:** marker; use a ### Changed (breaking) heading instead' — the stale-tree window); --next 0.12.0 --quest-ref main -> exit 0; --next 0.12.0 --quest-ref=main -> exit 0. Mutation re-run (level 'patch' -> 'major'): predicted 9 of 23 red, actual 9 fail / 14 pass, the identical 9 (one-tree, bare-heading, finalized, hybrid-a, both-markers, quest-forces, real-tree, CLI patch, CLI quest-forces); restored, 23/23 green. Gates after the fix: bun test 4543 pass 1 skip 0 fail; bun run typecheck 0; bun run lint 0 (same 4 pre-existing warnings); bun run lore check 0.

REVIEWER PASS (2026-09-28, parent-recorded): opum-workflow:reviewer re-review verdict APPROVE on origin/feat/LCLI-632-breaking-bump-gate @ 2a9d5df7 vs origin/dev @ 634fa9e1. All three CHANGES-REQUIRED findings verified closed: (1) the version's own section now wins when it exists (quest's own !== -1 priority) - reproduced the hybrid tree through the real CLI, exit 1 naming the own section, and confirmed byte-parity with quest's script at bee16361 on six identical fixtures including message strings; (2) the X -> X self-patch mechanism is removed and unreachable, 'pass --next' gone from the tree; (3) the header and the release.yml comment state the precise rule, with the stale-tree window documented (no-flag run on a released version checks that released section and reds on lore's legacy marker - not reachable at CI dispatch). Also verified: --quest-ref=main equals form honored (and empty exits 2); recorded real-tree outputs reproduced at this head; level-comparison mutation 9-of-23 exact; legacy-marker check no regression; release.yml wiring + LCLI-616 scan green (57/57); gates 23/23, 57/57, typecheck 0, lore check 0, full bun test 4544 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail.

WINDOWS-ONLY CI RED (PR #379, run 36477182923, job 109113712220, windows-latest; run-wide 4 fail / 4262 pass / 295 skip), diagnosed and fixed by delegated-agent lore-cli-session (2026-09-28). The four failing tests are the stubbed-gh CLI tests in test/lcli632-breaking-bump-gate.test.ts, failing at lines 480, 499, 517, 547; the malformed---next test passed because it exits 2 before spawning gh. Verified from the job log, not inferred: the received stderr was the real gh.exe own refusal ("To use ... in an Actions workflow, set the GH_TOKEN environment variable") -- the REAL runner gh.exe ran, not the stub. Diagnosis: on Windows, execFile PATH resolution (PATHEXT) never matches an extensionless file, so the bare stub "gh" was skipped and the search fell through to the runner real gh.exe, whose failure took the script fail-closed unreadable-quest path and shifted every quest-side expectation.

FIX (test only; the release-prep script is unchanged): withStubGh is platform-aware. On win32 it writes a gh.cmd wrapper around the same sh body in a sibling gh.sh, which execFile resolves via PATHEXT and cmd.exe runs; on posix it keeps the bare executable gh. The FAKE_GH_* env vars are inherited through the wrapper chain, confirmed by the stub-driven tests.

SIMULATED PROOF (darwin, simulated win32): bun --preload faking process.platform plus a local child-side Windows PATH-resolution emulation (PATHEXT search over the stub bin; simulation artifacts live in a scratch dir, not part of the change). BEFORE the fix: exactly the same four red / 19 pass. AFTER: 23/23 pass under the simulated win32 AND 23/23 native darwin. MUTATION (posix stub forced under simulated win32): the same four red again, then undid the mutation and re-ran green. Gates at this head: full bun test 4560 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail (exit 0); tsc noEmit 0; biome lint 0 (same 4 pre-existing warnings, none in this file); lore docs gate exit 0 (82 files, 0 errors).

WINDOWS RED #2, ROOT CAUSE AND FIX (2026-09-28, parent). The gh.cmd wrapper did NOT work on the real runner: run 36490045542 (head f82b4f10) failed the same four CLI tests, and the failing stderr shows the RUNNER'S REAL gh.exe answering ('To use GitHub CLI in a GitHub Actions workflow, set the GH_TOKEN environment variable'). Measured cause: the script spawns a bare 'gh' via execFile, and on Windows CreateProcess appends only '.exe' when resolving a bare name, so it walks past an extensionless stub AND past gh.cmd (Node additionally refuses to spawn a .cmd without shell:true since the CVE-2024-27980 hardening). No PATH stub can shadow the runner's gh.exe. The local win32 simulation was a false green for this class - it modelled the child's resolution rather than CreateProcess's. FIX, following this repository's own precedent: version-parity.test.ts - whose script makes the same gh-by-ref read - wraps its PATH-stub CLI tests in describePosix (process.platform === 'win32' ? describe.skip : describe); LCLI-632's four CLI tests now do the same, and the dead win32 branch of the stub helper is deleted. Compensating coverage on Windows: the in-process readQuestChangelog tests inject execFile directly and run on every platform, and the verdict/parse tests are pure functions; only the argv-and-exit-code path through the real command is posix-only, exactly as version-parity already accepts.

PRECISION on the posix-only change (2026-09-28, parent): the stubbed-gh describe holds FIVE tests, not four — the four that need the stub, plus 'a malformed --next exits 2' which passed on Windows because it exits before spawning gh and is now also skipped there. Faked-win32 run as the control (bun --preload, process.platform = win32): 18 pass, 5 skip, 0 fail — so the four windows reds become skips and the in-process tests (the compensating coverage) still run and pass under win32. Native darwin: 23 pass, 0 fail. Head ef7b1f7a.
finalSummary: Delivered via opum-ai/lore-cli#379, CI run 36490832395 (all five required dev contexts green on head 69e48fdd). scripts/check-breaking-bump.mjs gates release prep: a patch-level bump is refused when the notes for the version being released carry a '### ... (breaking)' heading, or lore's legacy bold behaviour-change marker (refusal names the canonical spelling). Section selection is quest-cli's own-section-priority rule, verified byte-identical against their script at bee16361 by execution on identical fixtures. The gate also reads quest-cli's CHANGELOG by ref (--quest-ref, default dev, equals form accepted) and refuses on an unreadable or zero-section quest changelog; release.yml's new breaking-bump job gates publish. AC1-4 all checked; reviewer APPROVE on re-review (2a9d5df7) after a CHANGES-REQUIRED certification-hole finding was fixed. Windows: the CLI PATH-stub tests are posix-only per the version-parity precedent (CreateProcess appends only .exe, so no stub can shadow the runner's gh.exe; measured twice on CI), with the logic covered on Windows by the in-process execFile tests.
